ground_truth: The ball constantly falls on the spring board and triggers it. As soon the blimp reaches it the spring board triggers a diagonal fly
response:
Because the blimp was sitting on a curved surface. The blimp produces an upward buoyant force, but when it rests against the curved arch the contact (normal) force is not straight down — it has a sideways component. When the blimp breaks contact that sideways component (plus any small overlap/impulse from the physics solver) gives it a horizontal velocity as well as vertical, so it leaves at a diagonal.

Fixes: put the blimp on a flat horizontal surface (or centered so it doesn’t touch the arch edge) or move it slightly away from the arch so it can rise without being pushed sideways.
